propositions: A configured provider is silently discarded when a model ID contains a colon (as in canonical versioned Bedrock IDs like 'anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0'), because _resolve_target tests '":" in model' to detect already-qualified strings and incorrectly returns unqualified IDs

Downstream parsing treats an unqualified versioned Bedrock ID as provider:model by splitting on the first colon, causing infer_provider to extract a fragment of the model ID (e.g. 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1') and report it as an unknown provider

The error message contradicts the operator's configuration, reporting a non-existent provider (a fragment of the model ID) instead of naming the actual misconfiguration, masking the root cause from diagnostics

Two independent implementations of the same qualifier-detection logic (_resolve_target and infer_provider) drift in their behavior, leading to silent double-prefix drops for non-identifier prefixes like 'openai:gpt-4o' when provider='bedrock' is configured
Guard order is incorrect: the presence of a colon in a model string is tested before a configured provider is checked, allowing punctuation to override explicit configuration
